info.title: The Selling Partner API for Messaging Automations
info.description: The Selling Partner API for Messaging Automations allows sellers to programmatically manage automated buyer-seller messaging configurations. An automation configuration defines rules for automatically responding to buyer messages (for example, auto-responses to common questions about shipping, returns, or product details). A seller can create multiple automation configurations, and each configuration can apply to one or more Amazon stores. Each store-specific entry within a configuration contains the response content and the automation trigger conditions. The `marketplaceIds` query parameter is required on all operations for store-scoped authorization.

post.description: Creates a new automation configuration for automated buyer-seller messaging. The configuration is `ACTIVE` as soon as it is created. The response returns the full automation configuration resource, including the server-generated `automationId`.

Required for store-scoped operations and authorization. Your application must have permission to operate in the specified stores before processing the request body.

put.description: Updates an existing automation configuration. This is a full replacement operation using `PUT` semantics; you must provide the complete desired state, including `automationDisplayName`, `automationStatus`, and `marketplaceAutomations`. The `marketplaceAutomations` entries you provide replace all of the configuration's existing Amazon store entries; any store that you omit is removed from the configuration. To deactivate a configuration, send its complete current state with `automationStatus` set to `DEACTIVATED`.

parameters.name: automationId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the automation configuration to update.

parameters.name: marketplaceIds
parameters.description: A comma-delimited list of [Amazon store identifiers](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/marketplace-ids) for the request. Required for store-scoped operations and authorization. Your application must have permission to operate in the specified stores before processing the request body.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The request body for updating an automation configuration.

AutomationConfiguration.description: Represents a seller's automation configuration for automated buyer-seller messaging. An automation configuration defines rules for automatically responding to buyer inquiries, such as common questions about shipping, returns, or product details. Each configuration has a type (for example, `AUTO_RESPONSE`), a status (`ACTIVE` or `DEACTIVATED`), and one or more store-specific entries that contain the actual response content and trigger conditions.

automationId.description: The unique identifier of the automation configuration.

automationDisplayName.description: The seller-provided display name for the automation configuration.

currentAutomationVersion.description: The version number of the automation configuration that is currently serving buyer messages. The version number increases by one with each update.

latestAutomationVersion.description: The most recent version number of the automation configuration. Because updates take effect immediately, this value always equals `currentAutomationVersion`.

marketplaceAutomations.description: A list of store-specific automation entries. Each entry contains the response content and trigger conditions for a specific Amazon store. Populated only for the `listAutomationConfigurations` operation when the `includeMarketplaceAutomations` query parameter is set to `true`.

createdDateTime.description: The date and time when the automation configuration was created, in ISO 8601 format.

lastUpdatedDateTime.description: The date and time when the automation configuration was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

MarketplaceAutomation.description: The store-specific entry within an automation configuration. A seller can have multiple automation configurations, and each configuration can contain entries for one or more Amazon stores. Each store entry defines the automation response content (for example, the auto-response text) and the trigger conditions (for example, specific buyer contact topics or ASINs) for that specific store.

AutomationDetails.description: The details of the automated action.

autoResponseText.description: The auto-response message text sent to the buyer. Required for `AUTO_RESPONSE` automation configurations.
autoResponseText.example: Thank you for reaching out. We typically respond within 24 hours. In the meantime, please check our storefront for common questions about shipping and returns.

autoResponseAttachmentUrl.description: A URL to an attachment included with the auto-response message.

TriggerConditions.description: The conditions that determine when an automation configuration activates for a given store. All conditions must be met simultaneously using `AND` logic. Within list-based conditions (such as `buyerContactTopics` or `asinList`), any single match satisfies that condition using `OR` logic. For example, if `buyerContactTopics` contains `SHIPPING` and `WHERES_MY_STUFF`, the automation triggers when the buyer's inquiry matches either topic. Trigger conditions cannot overlap with another active automation configuration in the same store; if any combination of ASIN, buyer contact topic, and buyer contact type is already covered by another active configuration, the request is rejected with a `409` error.

asinList.description: The ASINs this automation configuration applies to. The configuration only triggers for buyer inquiries about these ASINs. ASINs are validated for format only (10 alphanumeric characters); they are not checked against the catalog. Non-existent ASINs won't match a buyer inquiry.

AutomationType.description: The primary category of the automation configuration. Determines the kind of automated action performed when trigger conditions are met.

AutomationSubType.description: The sub-type of automation configuration. Used in combination with `automationType` to support future automation categories (for example, different types of auto-responses or refund automations). Currently, the only supported value is `AUTO_RESPONSE`.

x-docgen-enum-table-extension.description: An automated response sent to buyers when they contact the seller.

AutomationStatus.description: The current status of the automation configuration. A configuration is `ACTIVE` as soon as it is created. The auto-response text is validated when you create a configuration or update it with `automationStatus` set to `ACTIVE`. A request that contains text that is not permitted is rejected with a `422` error. Set the status to `DEACTIVATED` to stop the configuration from activating without deleting it, and reset it to `ACTIVE` to resume it.

CreateAutomationConfigRequest.description: The request body for creating a new automation configuration. A seller can have up to 10 automation configurations, including deactivated configurations.

automationDisplayName.description: A display name for the automation configuration. The name must be unique (case-insensitive) among the seller's automation configurations.

marketplaceAutomations.description: A list of store-specific automation entries. Each entry specifies the store, the response content, and the trigger conditions for that store.

UpdateAutomationConfigRequest.description: The request body for updating an existing automation configuration.

automationDisplayName.description: An updated display name for the automation configuration. To keep the current name, provide the existing value.
